searchText: Hello, I have a doubt over RLP encoding and decoding in transaction.go (https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/master/core/types/transaction.go#L102) Currently transaction struct only has `inner` as another element which is being encoded. What if transaction struct had two fields (e.g. `inner1` & `inner2`)? How exactly would encoding and decoding would work? Will we need to encode them one by one and while decoding also one by one or some other approach? There are custom encoding and decoding methods that are internally called by the rlp encoder (EncodeRLP, DecodeRLP) Yes that's where my doubt is. The custom encoding method for EncodeRLP is called encodeTyped() which writes tx type and then encodes tx.inner(rlp.Encode(w, tx.inner)). So if there's an inner2, can I simply do rlp.Encode(w, tx.inner2) right after encoding the inner1? You could, yes

Hello,
I have a doubt over RLP encoding and decoding in transaction.go (https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/master/core/types/transaction.go#L102)
Currently transaction struct only has `inner` as another element which is being encoded. What if transaction struct had two fields (e.g. `inner1` & `inner2`)? How exactly would encoding and decoding would work?
Will we need to encode them one by one and while decoding also one by one or some other approach?

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: There are custom encoding and decoding methods that are internally called by the rlp encoder (EncodeRLP, DecodeRLP)

excerpts.author: satyajitsato
excerpts.content: Yes that's where my doubt is. The custom encoding method for EncodeRLP is called encodeTyped() which writes tx type and then encodes tx.inner(rlp.Encode(w, tx.inner)). So if there's an inner2, can I simply do rlp.Encode(w, tx.inner2) right after encoding the inner1?
